title: Impact of Energy Crisis on Hiring Prospects
what_it_is: Impact of Energy Crisis on Hiring Prospects

sections.label: Firms' hiring intention survey
sections.summary: MOM's survey shows firms intending to hire fell from 54.6% in February 2026 to 44.6% in March 2026, with early signs of stabilisation in April.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Based on the Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) survey, the proportion of firms intending to hire in the next three months, fell from 54.6% in February 2026 to 44.6% in March 2026.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Although expectations remain below February's levels, there were early signs of stabilisation in April.

sections.label: Work Pass policy calibration
sections.summary: The Ministry was asked whether it intends to further calibrate Work Pass policies if Singaporeans, particularly mid-career PMETs, face weaker hiring, and said it has not seen shifts in firms' hiring preferences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And does the Ministry intend to further calibrate Work Pass policies if Singaporeans, particularly mid-career professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs), are facing disproportionately weaker hiring process?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have not seen any shifts at the moment in firms' hiring preferences.

sections.label: Employment Pass and S Pass salaries
sections.summary: At Budget and the Committee of Supply this year, an increase in Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salaries was announced, taking effect from January 2027.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For example, at Budget and the Committee of Supply this year, we announced an increase in Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salaries that will take effect from January 2027.

sections.label: Crisis and structural shifts
sections.summary: The view is that the crisis is likely to accelerate existing structural shifts already underway in the entire global economy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Our view is that the crisis is likely to accelerate the existing structural shifts that are already underway in the entire global economy.

sections.label: Singapore as trusted hub
sections.summary: Singapore's strategic position, goodwill, trust, credibility and reputation will be tested by the crisis, and prevailing would consolidate its position as a trusted hub; the Prime Minister committed to no export restriction, sectors will remain relevant, and decarbonisation targets remain.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For Singapore, because we stand at a very strategic crossroad between the East and the West, I believe that given the decades of goodwill, the trust, the credibility and our reputation that we have built as a very reliable partner to many countries, this crisis will test us and if we are able to prevail, I think, it would cement, reinforce and consolidate our position as a trusted hub.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, to that end, our Prime Minister has, in recent weeks, committed that we will not impose any export restriction.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And our sectors here will continue to see relevance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And of course, we are equally committed to our decarbonisation targets that we have set for ourselves.

sections.label: Economic Strategy Review report
sections.summary: The speaker read the draft of the Economic Strategy Review report, which is going to be released soon.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I had the opportunity of reading the draft of the Economic Strategy Review report.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I think it is going to be released soon.
